prompt: Solve $\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ for $0^\circ \le \theta < 360^\circ$. What is the SMALLER of the two solutions, in degrees?
hint: Ignore the sign to get the reference angle: $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, so it is $30^\circ$.

hints.text: Ignore the sign to get the reference angle: $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, so it is $30^\circ$.
Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.
Quadrant III: $180^\circ + 30^\circ = 210^\circ$. Quadrant IV: $360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ$. The smaller is $210^\circ$.

explanation: The reference angle comes from $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, so it is $30^\circ$.
A negative sine means the point on the unit circle is below the axis: quadrants III and IV.
Those angles are $180^\circ + 30^\circ = 210^\circ$ and $360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ$; the smaller is $210^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A note on the calculator answer
steps: A calculator returns $\arcsin(-0.5) = -30^\circ$, which is not in the required interval.
Add $360^\circ$ to it and you get $330^\circ$, one of the answers.
The other, $210^\circ$, never appears on the calculator screen — you must find it yourself from the reference angle. This is why the unit circle matters.
